feature: Automatic enable/disable handoff and viewport
notes: Assistant must recognize the installation and own the virtual display; in-world geometry must match.

feature: Windowed transition and native window-mode restoration
notes: Uses client CVars plus the Windows Assistant; server/client restrictions can differ.

feature: Automatic gameplay UI scale and custom scale slider
notes: Original scale restored on exit; separate from dashboard/controller scaling.

feature: Convert current native Edit Mode layout
notes: Retail/Forever use native Edit Mode conversion; Era/Mists apply the saved Classic preset. Automatic repositioning is disabled for other Classic builds.

feature: Keep viewport after reload and map transitions
notes: Implemented resume/recovery paths; real reconnect timing is client-dependent.

feature: Hide WoWU outside gamepad mode; show/hide commands
notes: Manual /wowushow remains available; normal startup is hidden.

feature: Restore minimap, decorations and native controls
notes: Mode owns the map only while viewport active. Positions, masks, visibility and collected addon controls restore.

feature: Three saved editable widget layouts
notes: Move/resize, choose widgets and save per-profile settings; secure changes wait for combat to end.

feature: Minimap with inset zone name
notes: Square mask while docked; original mask restored afterward.

feature: Clock, calendar, tracking, zoom and addon-controls widget
notes: Native controls appear where the client provides them; no calendar is invented for Era. Horizontal/vertical arrangement supported.

feature: Quest tracker widget
notes: Era/Mists use independent WoWU watches; other clients use their quest/watch APIs.

feature: Quick Access grid, single buttons and multiple instances
notes: Items/spells/mounts; row/column sizing, centered single button and press-and-hold reorder. Actual actions require native support and user input.

feature: Damage/healing meter widget
notes: Requires native C_DamageMeter; no independent combat-log parser. Missing API means no readings.

feature: Dungeon Hub widget
notes: Shared presentation; meter, threat and instance information require the corresponding native APIs.

feature: XP, money, bag-space and durability widgets
notes: Read-only information; unavailable/max-level XP is handled separately.

feature: Emotes and keyboard widget/buttons
notes: Keyboard writes to supported edit fields; sending/confirming remains a user action.

feature: Notifications hidden when idle
notes: Alert card is hidden with no current alert; full history remains accessible through Adventure.

feature: Independent four-layer controller assignments
notes: No trigger, LT, RT, LT+RT. Forever retains its own native controller implementation. Other Classic controller APIs need validation.

feature: Compact eight-button controller HUD
notes: WoWU HUD layers occupy one pair. Forever uses its own HUD rather than WoWU Compact Layout.

feature: Controller cluster/pair edit mode and scaling
notes: Four-button diamonds or eight-button pairs; changes outside combat. Forever uses its native controls.

feature: Pressed-button illumination and refined button frames
notes: Cosmetic WoWU HUD feedback uses mapped physical input. Native Forever styling is separate.

feature: Yellow animated proc borders
notes: Only when the client exposes public native proc signals. No guessed procs from buffs or cooldowns; Era generally lacks these signals.

feature: Hold to Cast repeated casting
notes: Off by default. Requires native held-casting APIs/CVar and spell on an existing action bar, even a hidden bar. Items/macros stay single-press. Forever uses native behavior.

feature: LB/RB targeting layers, friendly/enemy cycling and Back
notes: WoWU secure shoulder layers for Retail/Classic; Forever native bindings are not replaced. Combat restrictions apply.

feature: Ground-targeted spell aiming
notes: Native cursor/free-look APIs and secure click emulation required. Cannot certify targeting in a mock environment.

feature: Vehicle/possessed action replacement
notes: Requires matching native action-page APIs. Pet/stance/vehicle UI differs by client.

feature: Specific Skyriding button mapping
notes: RT+A ascent, RT+X forward, RT+Y surge, RT+B halt; LT+A Second Wind. Other layers preserved.

feature: Spellbook with paging, swipes and click inspector
notes: Uses private Classic API adapter where needed. No drag-to-action-bar requirement.

feature: +Pad and +Dashboard assignment actions
notes: Dashboard pins are shared. +Pad requires the WoWU controller preset; Forever native pad-assignment flow is separate.

feature: Item inspector, equipped comparison and concise stat changes
notes: Equipment comparisons only for gear; statistics and equipped slots depend on native data.

feature: Character model, equipment, statistics and currencies
notes: Model/stat data and supported currency/reputation APIs vary by client.

feature: Inventory grid, adjustable icon sizes and item actions
notes: Use/equip/split/drop/protection through hardware-driven native actions; swipe gestures avoid dragging.

feature: Bag cleanup/sorting
notes: Classic uses WoWU one-move-at-a-time sorter. Retail uses native cleanup. Forever follows its supported cleanup API.

feature: Bank split view and selected-item transfers
notes: Custom banking is explicitly Retail-only. Other clients retain native banking rather than this custom two-panel transfer UI.

feature: Native bank-window docking fallback
notes: Legacy/native bank interaction remains available; this is not the Retail custom transfer interface.

feature: Reagent deposits and purchasable tabs in custom bank
notes: Retail custom bank features depend on supported native reagent/tab APIs. Legacy bank slot purchases use native windows instead.

feature: Warband bank and shared-money deposits
notes: Retail only, subject to current bank/tab APIs and account unlocks.

feature: Merchant catalogue, buy/sell/buyback and repair
notes: Requires open merchant; purchasing still needs a user action.

feature: Mailbox in bags, attachments, money and keyboard
notes: Requires native mail APIs and open mailbox; COD/confirmation restrictions remain.

feature: Custom Auction House browse, categories, buy, sell and owned auctions
notes: Retail/Forever use modern AH when available; Classic uses the legacy backend. Native permissions and commodity differences remain.

feature: AH scan cache and tooltip prices
notes: Legacy full scans are throttled by the client; modern AH uses eligible queries/results rather than a guaranteed whole-realm GetAll scan. Prices are last-seen observations per realm/client.

feature: Parchment quest journal, objectives and rewards
notes: Uses private legacy quest adapter where necessary.

feature: Track/untrack, Navigate, Show on Map and confirmed Abandon
notes: Quest position/area navigation needs native quest POIs or a supported database. Abandon uses a confirmation.

feature: World map and touch navigation
notes: Retail map chrome removed; Era/Mists custom art and navigation paths. Other Classic clients use generic native-map fallback.

feature: Mists numbered quest pins and highlighted objective areas
notes: Mists-specific POI selection links to WoWU quest tracking.

feature: Compass headings and destination indicators
notes: Uses camera-facing API where available; direct navigation needs public position data. Player-facing fallback may apply if the client lacks camera data.

feature: Quest, destination and corpse trails
notes: Direct guidance only: does not calculate road/pathfinding routes. Classic quest locations are strongest for the dedicated Era/Mists adapters.

feature: Services, rares, treasures and notable-place catalogues
notes: 59,361 guarded coordinate records across seven profiles. Coverage is source-dependent; not a claim to every known live spawn/location. No gathering-node import.

feature: Map filters, swipe destination list and destination details
notes: Services/Places menus, Rares, Saved, Explored and search; source markers/availability depend on profile.

feature: Saved map positions/pins and explored-location log
notes: Personal observations; not a complete historical exploration database. Requires native map positioning.

feature: Talent selection and specialization UI
notes: Retail custom class/spec trees; Mists custom six-tier one-per-row selector and specialization previews. Earlier Classic docks native talents. Forever uses its custom trees.

feature: Retail specialization cards and activation
notes: Retail free-spec switching follows native restrictions and available API.

feature: Forever Legacy trees
notes: Explicitly Forever-only.

feature: Profession cards and recipe crafting screen
notes: Retail/Forever current profession UI; Mists legacy recipe adapter. Earlier Classic docks native profession windows.

feature: Mining opens Smelting; gathering cards are noninteractive
notes: Profession/API-specific; pre-Mists native hosting does not share every custom-card refinement.

feature: Cooking Fire action in custom cooking view
notes: Custom cooking view offers learned Cooking Fire; earlier Classic profession hosting does not provide this WoWU button.

feature: Disenchant, Milling and Prospecting item tools
notes: Requires learned profession/spell and an eligible selected item. Milling/Prospecting are unavailable in versions that lack those professions.

feature: Clickable reagent inspector, source hints and AH prices
notes: Source hints/examples are not exhaustive. Prices need a local scan; pre-Mists native profession windows do not share every custom reagent control.

feature: Fishing Companion session/catch view
notes: Retail/Mists custom entry. Earlier Classic profession routing is native; Forever fishing possession is not wired to its own controller preset.

feature: Retail Cast/Reel In button
notes: Cast uses Fishing; Reel In uses the native interact binding, requiring client interaction settings/bobber eligibility.

feature: Fishing control possession and stick remapping
notes: Mists uses A cast, X reel, temporary left-stick cursor and movement lock. Requires WoWU controller mode plus device remap APIs; earlier Classic lacks a dedicated profession entry.

feature: Mount and companion collections
notes: Era/TBC use inventory/learned companion fallback; later clients use available journals. Actual summon uses secure actions.

feature: Appearance browser with paged model previews and zoom
notes: Retail/Forever transmog APIs; Classic collection implementation does not expose appearances. Only visible-page metadata/model work is requested.

feature: Toys browser, large icon, inspector and Use Toy
notes: Requires toy-journal APIs. Classic collection tabs do not expose this toy browser.

feature: Integrated NPC dialogue, quest offers, progress and rewards
notes: Possesses the current module content while the interaction is open, with native close/back behavior.

feature: Trainer and other NPC-window docking
notes: Uses interaction-manager enums where available, legacy show/hide events for Classic. Protected/unsupported windows may require native use.

feature: Transmogrifier docking
notes: Only if the client supplies a transmogrifier window; standard Era/TBC/Wrath do not supply this service.

feature: Trading Post docking
notes: Retail PerksProgram frame only; native purchase/cart controls remain native.

feature: Adventure alerts, larger readable log and history
notes: History access corrected for Era/TBC/Wrath in v0.13.2. User option gating and per-character bounded history.

feature: Mail, bag space, repair, talent and upgrade reminders
notes: Only when corresponding game APIs/events and enabled notification categories supply data. Upgrade hints do not auto-equip.

feature: Queue, group, summon, resurrection and ready-check prompts
notes: Actual native prompts are positioned on WoWU; acceptance remains a user action. Queueing systems differ by expansion.

feature: Auction, crafting completion, fishing lure and calendar notices
notes: API/event-dependent. Calendar reminders need a calendar; crafting notices need successful craft events.

feature: Custom social/chat UI and keyboard
notes: Friends, guild, chat, invite and target actions only where their native APIs are available; network/account services are client-dependent.

feature: Achievements
notes: Classic module visibility starts at Wrath. Forever availability follows its actual achievement API.

feature: Custom Dungeon Journal / Adventure Guide
notes: Named Dungeon Journal in Mists; Adventure Guide in Retail. Cata uses native hosting. Forever tile is currently hidden, despite bundled Compendium code/data.

feature: Dungeon Finder, raids, roles and queue controls
notes: Mists/Retail custom views; progression Classic uses native hosting. Forever retains its own native systems.

feature: PvP pages inside Dungeon Finder
notes: Dedicated Mists Casual/Rated/War Games paths. The Retail custom finder currently has no PvP tab; earlier progression uses native hosting.

feature: Housing Dashboard and Shop shortcuts
notes: Retail shortcuts open Blizzard windows; no custom commerce implementation. Housing requires a client build with the feature.

feature: Floating loot pickup feed and fast loot
notes: Optional existing QoL feed; not the removed duplicate loot-feed module. Native loot information is required.

feature: Optional auto-sell, repair and mail collection
notes: Opt-in bounded convenience actions; native permissions, protected items, COD and purchase confirmations are respected.
